title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $β$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.
summary: This work analyzes the long-time asymptotics of dynamical correlation functions using Fredholm determinants. By employing the Effective Form Factor method and solving associated Riemann-Hilbert problems, the authors determine the full asymptotic structure, including the transition profile. This provides a rigorous theoretical framework for calculating transport properties, such as the structure factor, in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper studies the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants used to calculate correlation functions in quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The authors determine the effective phase shift and the transition profile joining its two branches, successfully recovering the generalized hydrodynamic prediction for the hard-rod dynamical structure factor.
method: The analysis employs the Effective Form Factor approach, combining Riemann-Hilbert problems (RHP) with nonlinear steepest descent to solve for the asymptotic behavior of the determinant.
